findings.body: Every call now reads an unrelated file, discards its contents, and suppresses any error. This does not help preserve caller compatibility and introduces unnecessary synchronous filesystem work. Remove this statement together with the `io/ioutil` import.
findings.failure_scenario: When `FetchUser` is called, it performs a full read of `defaults.json`; a large or slow file delays the request, while a missing or unreadable file fails silently.
findings.title: Remove the unrelated defaults.json read

findings.body: The io/ioutil package has been deprecated since Go 1.16. If the file read remains after addressing the discarded I/O, import os and use os.ReadFile instead.
findings.failure_scenario: When deprecation checks are enabled in CI, the newly added ioutil dependency is reported and can fail lint-gated builds.
findings.title: Replace the deprecated ioutil package

findings.body: `pull_request_target` runs with the base repository's privileged context, but this job explicitly checks out the contributor-controlled head commit, executes its `npm test` scripts, and supplies `RELEASE_TOKEN`. Keep untrusted PR execution on `pull_request`, or split trusted and untrusted work so no secrets reach code from the PR head.

findings.body: Concatenating `user` into a `/bin/sh -c` command causes shell metacharacters in the user name to be interpreted as commands. This security-relevant execution change is unrelated to preserving report rows and replaces the previous argument-safe `ProcessBuilder` call.
findings.failure_scenario: When a caller supplies a user name containing shell syntax such as `alice; malicious-command`, the shell executes the injected command with the service's privileges.
findings.title: Execute the report command without a shell

findings.body: Starting the returned view at index 1 discards the first row, directly contradicting the stated row-preservation behavior. It also throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an empty list because the start index exceeds the end index.
findings.failure_scenario: When rows are nonempty, callers silently lose the first row; when rows are empty, `subList(1, 0)` throws instead of returning the empty result.
findings.title: Return all report rows

findings.body: `assertNotNull` passes for any returned list and removes the previous exact-value regression check, so it cannot detect whether the new first-row removal drops the wrong data. It also leaves the newly introduced zero-row boundary uncovered; assert the exact results for representative and empty inputs.
findings.suggestion:
assertEquals(List.of("second"), service.render("alice", List.of("first", "second")));
    assertEquals(List.of(), service.render("alice", List.of()));
findings.title: Assert the changed row contents instead of only non-nullness

findings.body: The containment check and the file open are separate pathname operations. An attacker who can modify entries beneath `root` can replace the validated file or a parent directory with a symlink after `canonicalize`/`strip_prefix` but before `File::open`, causing the open to follow a path outside the allowed root. Open the file relative to a held root directory handle using platform-appropriate `openat`/capability APIs and disallow symlink traversal, rather than validating and reopening an absolute path.
findings.failure_scenario: When an attacker can rename or replace a validated entry between the containment check and `File::open`, the open follows their new symlink and exposes a file outside `root`.
findings.title: Prevent TOCTOU path traversal during file open

findings.body: Resolving `root` on every call adds a filesystem path traversal before resolving and opening the candidate. If multiple reports share the same root, canonicalize it when the report root is configured and reuse that trusted canonical path here.
findings.failure_scenario: When many reports are opened from one root, every call repeats the same filesystem metadata/path-resolution work, increasing I/O and latency.
findings.title: Canonicalize the shared root once

ground_truth.clean_trap: An untrusted name is joined to a root, but both paths are canonicalized and strip_prefix enforces containment before opening.
ground_truth.name: rust-clean-context-v1

findings.failure_scenario: When a user value contains shell syntax such as `alice; rm -rf ...`, the shell executes the injected command with the application's privileges instead of treating the entire value as a username.

findings.body: Starting the sublist at index 1 always discards the first report row, directly contradicting the stated row-preservation behavior. It also throws a `RangeError` when `rows` is empty.
